title: Introduction to Private Law (Prof. Dr. Roman Schister)
info: **Objectives:** understand the basics of Swiss private law and analyse contractual and tort law issues, detecting the legal difficulties and drafting concise, legally substantiated solutions.
- **Structure:** lectures; six in-person exercise sessions with cases (prepare literature and lecture beforehand); three online formative assessments with exam-type questions.
- **Bring the St.Gallen Compilation of Statutes (CC and CO)** to every lecture: working with the legal texts is an important part of exam preparation.
- **Mandatory reading:** Roberto/Schister, *Introduction to Business Law I: Contract Law and Liability* (8th ed., 2023). Not among your PDFs.
- Your PDFs cover Lectures **1–4**, plus a validity-of-contracts summary, an L4 study guide and two exercise sheets (questions only).

questions.question: Which defect makes a contract null and void rather than contestable?
questions.explanation: Capacity, consensus, form, content → void; defects of intent and unfair advantage → contestable.

questions.question: Both parties actually meant the same bike, although the buyer misspelled its name in the email. Result?
options: Natural consensus on the bike both meant
Normative consensus on the misspelled bike

questions.question: Within what time must a party contest a contract concluded through fraud?
options: One year from discovery of the fraud (CO 31)
questions.explanation: Error and fraud: from discovery; duress: from its end.

questions.question: Paul has bought pastries every Friday for years in his lecturer's name at the same bakery. The lecturer now refuses to pay, saying he never authorized Paul. Which concept protects the bakery?
options: Appearance of authority created by the principal (CO 33 III)
questions.explanation: A bona fide third party can rely on an appearance of authority attributable to the principal.

questions.question: Eva's dog salon trims Bello as Hanna instructed, to be picked up in an hour. Which contract?
questions.explanation: A specific result (the grooming) is owed.

questions.question: A landlord claims unpaid rent six years after it became due. Rent is a periodic claim. Which is correct?
options: 5-year period (CO 128), claim prescribed and no longer enforceable
questions.explanation: Periodic claims: 5 years; prescription makes a claim unenforceable.

questions.question: In a sales contract, the price risk is governed primarily by…
options: CO 185 (as a special rule under CO 119 III)

questions.question: An ambiguous GTC clause is interpreted…
options: against the drafter (in dubio contra stipulatorem)

questions.question: Name the four requirements of direct agency and the consequence of valid agency. Then explain what happens if an agent acts without authority (two possibilities for the principal, and the agent's liability).
questions.model: Requirements: (1) authority (power of attorney, CO 33, or by law), (2) acting in the name of another person (explicit, implied, or third party indifferent, CO 32 II), (3) the transaction allows for agency, (4) the agent is capable of judgment. Consequence (CO 32 I): the rights and obligations accrue to the principal, not the agent. Without authority: the contract is pending; the principal may ratify it (CO 38) and then is bound, or refuse. If not ratified, the agent is liable to the third party for damages (CO 39): negative contractual interest, or, if the agent was at fault, positive contractual interest is possible. (Good-faith third parties may be protected by CO 33 III, 34 III, 37 I.)

keyPoints.text: CO 32 I consequence (rights/obligations accrue to principal)
CO 39: agent's liability, negative interest; positive if at fault
Mentions good-faith protection (CO 33 III / 34 III / 37 I)

questions.question: On 3 October Anne sells Bertrand a unique lamp; he will collect it a week later. (a) On the night of 5–6 October lightning destroys it. (b) Alternative: on 5 October the cleaner hired by Anne knocks it over. For each, must Bertrand pay? Use the slide checklist.
questions.model: Checklist: contract concluded? accidental destruction? risk passed? (a) Contract concluded on 3 Oct. Lightning = accident. The lamp is a specific good; under CO 185 I benefit and risk pass at conclusion (no special circumstances or agreement) → the price risk is with Bertrand → he must pay, although his claim to delivery has ceased (CO 119 I). (b) Destruction by Anne's cleaner, i.e. an auxiliary person of the seller, is not an accident in the sense of the passing-of-risk rules → CO 185 does not apply; Anne is liable for breach of contract (CO 97, with CO 101 for auxiliary persons) → Bertrand need not pay and can claim damages.

keyPoints.text: (a) Specific good, CO 185 I risk at conclusion → Bertrand pays
(b) Not an accident (auxiliary person of the seller)
(b) CO 97 (101) instead of CO 185 → no payment / damages
